title: Who owns what you see
summary: A crowd of 64 participants closed participants within a minute: the world showed everything in range, and the gateway refused the 129th object. Visibility had no owner. Now the world chooses what each participant sees, by what matters to it.

title: The 4097th command
summary: After about seventy minutes of play, every action ended in an error. A promise that no command runs twice had been kept by remembering every command, until the memory was full.

title: The answer the world already knew
summary: An engage could end Unknown without ever reaching the world. The gateway inferred outcomes from what followed, while the world kept an exact record of what it did.

title: Three copies of the truth
summary: Between the world and a participant, three layers each kept their own picture of what the participant sees and their own queue. Most defects of the release lived where those copies met.

title: Reviving an abandoned MMO server: 2009 → 2026
summary: An archived Lineage II server became one Java 25 process on PostgreSQL 18, shipped as a signed image, one boundary at a time.

title: One process, hard boundaries
summary: Login and world in one process, kept apart by a two-interface contract and dependency rules checked at build time.

title: An island of our own
summary: The project deleted a game world it had not written and shipped a small one that it had, with a tool that checks every word of it.

title: One save, one transaction
summary: A character save and its item writes, grouped into one database transaction that commits or rolls back together.

title: Every merge is a release rehearsal
summary: Before an image may be published, the pipeline plays the first week of an operator's life with it.

title: Releases promote, never rebuild
summary: The release workflow has no build step: it verifies the image main already tested and gives that exact digest a version.

title: Starting a Java 25 server: G1, ZGC, and an AOT cache that did not help
summary: Where the start-up time of a Java 25 server goes, and why the AOT cache changed nothing.

title: Old bugs, new invariants
summary: The defect classes of a 2009 game server, the invariants that replaced them, and the checks that keep them out.
